title: A week of US outages, from a nationwide flight stop to banks; Rubio says there is "zero evidence" they are linked
seoTitle: US outages: FAA ground stop, Microsoft and banks explained
dek: The FAA halted departing flights across the US on 13 November, a day after a worldwide Microsoft outage, and banks and Apple services went down days later. Officials blame a faulty router installed by a contractor for the flight stop and say they see no sign of an attack.
happened: On Thursday, 12 November, a worldwide Microsoft outage hit Outlook and Teams; Microsoft linked it to a technical issue, not malicious activity. On Friday, 13 November, the Federal Aviation Administration halted all departing flights in the United States for several hours, disrupting thousands of flights. The outage happened during routine maintenance at a remote FAA site, where the agency's telecom contractor L3Harris was replacing old copper lines with fibre; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a router began flooding the FAA network with more than 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. Online services at JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and U.S. Bank were also disrupted, as were Apple services; both have since been restored. CBS News reports, citing several US officials, that an internal National Security Agency network used for classified information went offline on Tuesday, 17 November.

sides.who: The Transportation Department and the FAA
sides.says: Duffy said that at "at least one of our remote FAA locations, a contractor was doing routine maintenance", and that investigators are still working out "whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3 Harris", or faulty equipment. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said: "We see zero evidence of anything nefarious and zero evidence of anything AI-related."
The contractor says it has "completed more than 70% of the planned airspace communications conversion" from copper to fibre and "is supporting the FAA in its investigation".

Speaking in the Philippines on 18 November, he said: "These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another", and that there is "zero evidence" they are connected: "Each of them are distinct, and they're different in their causation." He said the US is not under systemic attack and declined to speculate on any role for AI.

Sen. Mark Warner, the Democratic vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, said there was no indication of an attack, but warned that "AI is making it possible to identify vulnerabilities across enormous numbers of systems at unprecedented speed" and called for "commonsense guardrails on AI".

next: The Transportation Department is investigating the ground stop with L3Harris taking part, and officials have not yet said whether it was human error, an installation mistake or faulty equipment. The other companies say their services are restored.
summary: In one week the US saw a worldwide Microsoft outage (12 November), a nationwide FAA halt on departing flights (13 November) and disruptions at major banks and Apple services. Officials blame the flight stop on a router installed during contractor maintenance and say they see no sign of malicious activity, and Secretary of State Rubio says there is "zero evidence" the outages are linked. The cause of the FAA failure is still under investigation.

conflicts: Cause of the FAA stop: CBS News says federal officials attributed it to a contractor doing maintenance updates but that key questions remain; Scripps reports Duffy saying a faulty router "might" be the cause and that human error, an installation mistake or faulty equipment have not been ruled out.
